note.after_visit_summary: You came in today because your ankles have been swelling and you've been gaining weight, feeling more short of breath than usual. We found that you have extra fluid in your body, likely from eating salty food at a recent wedding and taking naproxen for your knees, which can make heart failure worse. Your heart pump is weakened, as shown in prior tests. To help, we are stopping naproxen completely. For your knees, you can take acetaminophen 650 mg up to three times a day as needed. We are increasing your water pill (furosemide) to 40 mg twice a day for the next five days; once your weight returns to around 183 lbs, go back to 40 mg once a day. Keep taking all your other heart medications exactly as before. Weigh yourself every morning after using the bathroom and write it down. Try to eat less than 2,000 mg of salt per day and limit fluids to about 2 liters daily. We will check a blood test on the 21st of October to make sure your kidneys and potassium are handling the medication change well. Call us if your weight goes up by 3 lbs in one day or 5 lbs in one week. Go to the emergency room if you feel short of breath while resting or have chest pain. We will see you back in one week to check your weight and swelling. Instructions will be sent to your patient portal.
